newsitem.title: PERU: SOCCER-PERU OVERCOME CHILE IN ROUGH WORLD CUP QUALIFIER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PERU OVERCOME CHILE IN ROUGH WORLD CUP QUALIFIER.

text.p: Peru beat ten-man Chile 2-1 in a rough World Cup qualifying match on Sunday to keep alive their hopes of reaching the 1998 finals in France.
The win sent Peru into seventh-place in the single South American group. But they are only one point behind third-placed Argentina.
Peru created several early chances and were rewarded when striker Flavio Maestri pounced on a rebound in the 14th minute to head them in front.
Their second goal came in the 34th minute when Chile appeared to be on top, having hit the woodwork with an effort from Sebastian Rozental.
Maestri was again involved, providing the pass from which Roberto Palacios scored with a first time shot.
Chile, who had a player sent off last month as they drew 1-1 away to Argentina, had Fernando Cornejo shown the red card 12 minutes from the end for a foul on Nolberto Solano.
Two mintues from time, their top player Ivan Zamorano headed a consolation.

Peru - 1-Miguel Miranda, 7-Nolberto Solano, 3-Juan Reynoso, 6-Jose Soto, 4-Percy Olivares, 8-Juan Jayo Legario, 5-Roger Serrano, 16-Paolo Maldonado (17-Jose Pereda, 46th minunte), 10- Roberto Palacios, 9-Flavio Maestri (2-Jorge Soto, 79th), 11- Julinho (13-German Carty, 77th).

Chile - 1-Nelson Tapia, 2-Cristian Castaneda, 3-Juan Gonzales, 5-Pedro Reyes, 4-Marcelo Miranda, 6-Luis Musrry (17- Jaime Riveros, 57th), 7-Cristian Mora, 8-Fernando Cornejo, 22-Sebastian Rozental (10-Jorge Contreras, 81st), 9-Ivan Zamorano, 19-Fernando Vergara (18-Pedro Gonzalez, 63rd).
